# Susan Baker

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052)</sub>
- **Status:** alive  <sub>[v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052), [v4 c40 P49](../source/v04-c40.md#nw-v04-c40-p0049)</sub>
- **Origin:** the Glen  <sub>[v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052)</sub>
- **Role:** maid-of-all-work  <sub>[v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052)</sub>

## Appearance

Susan Baker is a grim-faced elderly spinster. She considers herself no beauty, though she feels she is as good-looking as most married women.

_Sources: [v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052), [v4 c22 P5](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0005)_

## Personality

Susan is a kind-hearted, pragmatic, and optimistic woman who prefers cheering people up over weeping. She takes immense pride in her culinary skills, particularly her baking, and dislikes it when others try to out-cook her. Though she is an old maid who never had a beau, she openly likes men and candidly enjoys seeing a good-looking man. She carries out her household duties with authority and remains deeply loyal to her family and employers.

_Sources: [v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052), [v4 c19 P41](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0041), [v4 c22 P3](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0003), [v4 c22 P5](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0005), [v4 c23 P5](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0005), [v4 c31 P13](../source/v04-c31.md#nw-v04-c31-p0013), [v4 c36 P21](../source/v04-c36.md#nw-v04-c36-p0021), [v4 c40 P49](../source/v04-c40.md#nw-v04-c40-p0049)_

- To manage the Doctor's household efficiently and serve Anne  <sub>[v4 c22 P3](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0003)</sub>
- To nurse and support her injured sister Matilda  <sub>[v4 c36 P21](../source/v04-c36.md#nw-v04-c36-p0021)</sub>

## History

Susan Baker was installed as the maid-of-all-work at the little house of Anne and Gilbert Blythe. When Anne took ill, Susan actively looked after her, taking offense when Cornelia Bryant brought food under the belief that her own cooking was superior. Gilbert insisted that Susan be retained for the summer to manage the household and look after Anne. Later, when her sister Matilda broke her leg, Susan temporarily departed her duties at the little house to care for her, despite noting that no one in her family had ever broken a leg before. She eventually returned to continue helping the doctor and his wife.

_Sources: [v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052), [v4 c19 P41](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0041), [v4 c22 P0](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0000), [v4 c22 P3](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0003), [v4 c36 P19](../source/v04-c36.md#nw-v04-c36-p0019), [v4 c36 P21](../source/v04-c36.md#nw-v04-c36-p0021), [v4 c38 P35](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0035), [v4 c40 P49](../source/v04-c40.md#nw-v04-c40-p0049)_

## Quotes

> You just take it easy, Mrs. Doctor, dear. Have a good time and do not worry about the pantry. Susan is at the helm.  <sub>[v4 c22 P3](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0003)</sub>

> I am an old maid, but you never hear ME abusing the men. I like ’em. I would have married one if I could.  <sub>[v4 c22 P5](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0005)</sub>
